text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add Claude Mythos 5 to EXCAVA's toolkit as the default model for creative reasoning tasks. This decision leverages its advanced capabilities in generating complex and nuanced outputs, which can enhance overall performance by addressing intricate user queries more effectively. The trade-off is the reliance on a newer model that may still require testing for reliability and integration, but the potential for improved task execution outweighs these initial uncertainties.

name: Torque
text: Claude Mythos 5’s "advanced capabilities" are irrelevant if EXCAVA’s core tasks don’t need creative reasoning—its real risk is wasted compute on tasks where precision beats flair. Default to the fastest model that meets accuracy thresholds; only switch to Mythos 5 for edge cases where nuance justifies the cost. Settle it by running a blind test: measure EXCAVA’s output quality on 50 live tasks with/without Mythos 5, no cherry-picking.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add Llama 3.3 70B to EXCAVA’s toolkit as the default high-precision reasoning model. Its 70B parameter size delivers better factual accuracy and logical consistency than smaller models, which directly raises EXCAVA’s capability for core tasks. The trade-off is higher compute cost per query, but we mitigate this by running it only when strict precision is required and falling back to lighter models otherwise.

name: Torque
text: Llama 3.3 70B’s compute cost isn’t the real risk—it’s the *latency ceiling* that caps EXCAVA’s throughput when users expect sub-second responses. Default to a distilled 8B-13B model fine-tuned for EXCAVA’s core tasks; only escalate to 70B for cases where the 8B flags uncertainty. Settle it with a 1000-query A/B test measuring both accuracy and p95 latency against the current baseline.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Run a 100-hour blind A/B bake-off on 5,000 live EXCAVA tasks comparing Llama 3.3 70B vs. Mistral Large 2 vs. Claude Mythos 5, defaulting to the fastest model that meets accuracy thresholds, escalating only when uncertainty is flagged—result must deliver quantified capability delta and latency impact; Torque owns execution and Torque owns the artifact.
